subject: ventures/eu-packaging-regulation-checker
professional: an EU packaging-compliance lawyer or EPR consultant who advises brand owners and non-EU online sellers on Regulation (EU) 2025/40, checking first: which economic-operator role the client has (manufacturer, producer, importer, distributor, fulfilment service provider, marketplace), the Article 71 application dates and every 'from X or N months after the implementing act, whichever is later' clause, the producer-register and authorised-representative duties (Articles 44-45), and the 2030 design duties with their exemptions (Article 7 recycled content, Article 24 empty space, Article 29 reuse targets and the cardboard-box and micro-enterprise carve-outs)

evidence.correctness: Ran the shipped calc.mjs through probes.mjs (scratchpad) and the page in headless Chrome. The primary text (EUR-Lex CELEX 32025R0040) could not be fetched: eur-lex.europa.eu is 403 at the proxy and not resolvable for WebFetch, so dates were checked against secondary sources found by web search (Latham & Watkins PPWR summary, Commission-guidance coverage in Packaging Europe, Reloop, Envirotec 2026-08-19, verpackungsregister.org, RegSurance timeline). Pass: general application, PFAS food-contact limits, conformity and producer registration from 2026-08-12 (Article 71; registration in existing national registers from that date); DRS from 2029-01-01; recyclability, recycled content, minimisation, empty space and single-use formats from 2030-01-01; day counts hand-checked (2026-11-17 -> 2028-08-12 = 634 days, -> 2030-01-01 = 1141, tool agrees). Fail: the DRS row says the exemption is 'a 90 percent separate-collection rate already met'; Article 50 sets 90% as the 2029 target and exempts a Member State reaching 80% in 2026 with a plan. Fail: the Article 29 40% reuse target covers transport packaging including e-commerce packaging, but the reuse row is limited to the transport category and to producer/importer/distributor, so the tool's own worked example (non-EU online seller, plastic mailers) shows no reuse duty; paper transport cartons get the reuse duty although cardboard boxes are excluded from the targets. Partial: label (2028-08-12), recycled content and empty space each run from the stated date 'or N months/years after the implementing act, whichever is later'; the label implementing act missed its 2026-08-12 deadline, so the 2028 date is already slipping, and the tool will flip it to 'applies now' on 2028-08-12. Reading-code cap does not apply (outputs run), but wrong rows on two duties hold correctness at 2.
evidence.completeness: Every README/page feature runs end to end: headless Chrome on a scratch copy loaded the example and rendered 'In scope — Gap: no EU operator', the summary text and three timeline rows (2026-08-12 applies now x2, 2030-01-01 later); done-markers, operator status, findings, text and CSV downloads are wired (page.test.mjs checks ids and the map). No TODOs or stubs. Served copy (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs) clean.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/eu-packaging-regulation-checker && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 30 tests, 30 pass, ~0.1 s. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (label date 2028 -> 2027, recycled-content dropping the multi-layer material, operator-gap condition flipped), 3 SURVIVED (DRS date 2029 -> 2030, the 'soon' window 365 -> 180 days, empty-space duty dropping transport packaging). No test pins the date of most duties or the category list of empty space and reuse, so the regulatory table can drift silently.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (172 lines), index.html script (lines 141-187), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Small pure engine, data-driven obligation table, page imports the engine (no copy), output escaped. Defects: header says 'Bad input is rejected with a message, never clamped' but opt() (calc.mjs:60-62) silently replaces unknown micro/sellsEu/euOperator values with defaults (micro='maybe' -> 'no'); done markers treat any truthy string except '0' as done, so 'false' marks a duty done (calc.mjs:81); default reference date is the UTC date (calc.mjs:75), one day off near midnight outside UTC. Acceptable to a senior reviewer with these noted.
evidence.claims: No-warranty and not-legal-advice footer (index.html:131), header note that dates were written from memory and can move (index.html:62), summary text repeats it (calc.mjs:165), README and VENTURE.yaml say the same and stage is 'prototype': the main limit is disclosed honestly. Privacy claim 'a test in the code asserts there are no network calls' is backed by page.test.mjs:20. Unbacked/wrong: the DRS row's 90 percent exemption (calc.mjs:48); FAQ says the empty-space rule 'applies from 1 January 2030' and the label 'from August 2028' without the later-of clause (index.html:121,123); llms.txt:5 says 'estimates from the numbers typed in' on a tool that takes no numbers (boilerplate).
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a non-EU Shopify seller shipping plastic mailers to EU buyers, and an EU brand owner of PET drinks. The tool correctly puts the seller in scope, flags the missing authorised representative and producer registration as overdue, which is the single most valuable answer for that user today. A compliance consultant would hit in the first hour: no Article numbers (deliberately omitted; the 'basis' column says 'labelling chapter'), single-select roles so an own-brand online seller choosing 'Online seller' loses conformity, label, recyclability and minimisation rows (probe P7), no online-marketplace or HORECA/take-away role (Articles 32-33 reuse offer from 2028), no compostable-packaging duty (2028), the reuse target missing for e-commerce, and no per-country register or fee guidance. Good first read for an SME, not a compliance plan.
evidence.domain: Against Regulation (EU) 2025/40 as summarised by law-firm and Commission-guidance sources: application dates and the duty list are mostly right and the authorised-representative logic matches Article 45(3). Departs: Article 50 exemption threshold (80% in 2026, not 90%); Article 29 reuse scope (e-commerce included, cardboard boxes excluded, micro-enterprise exemption is tied to the 1,000 kg per Member State per year condition per secondary sources, tool exempts any micro-enterprise); DRS shown for glass drinks bottles under the 'plastic bottle or metal can' category (probe P4); later-of implementing-act clauses for Articles 7, 12 and 24 not modelled; Article numbers omitted. A packaging lawyer would treat it as a reasonable checklist that needs those fixes and the EUR-Lex check its own README asks for before sign-off.

DRS shown for glass drinks bottles under a category labelled 'plastic bottle or metal can'; material is not cross-checked against the beverage category
Header promises bad input is rejected, but opt() silently replaces unknown micro/sellsEu/euOperator values and any string but '0' (e.g. 'false') marks a duty done

Dates never verified against EUR-Lex and Article numbers deliberately omitted; the 'basis' column gives chapter names only
llms.txt says results are 'estimates from the numbers typed in'; the tool takes no numbers

verdict: An honest, small PPWR first-read checklist that gets the headline right: for a non-EU online seller it says the Regulation applies now and that producer registration and an authorised representative are overdue, and its 2026, 2029 and 2030 dates agree with secondary legal summaries (EUR-Lex itself was unreachable from this session). Below the bar on correctness and domain: the Article 29 reuse target is missing for e-commerce packaging (including the tool's own worked example) and wrongly applied to cardboard transport boxes, the DRS exemption is stated as 90% instead of 80% in 2026, the later-of implementing-act clauses for the label, recycled content and empty space are not modelled though the label act has already slipped, and single-select roles drop design duties for own-brand online sellers. 30 tests pass but 3 of 6 seeded mutants survive. Disclaimers and the dates-from-memory disclosure are present and accurate. Finished (completeness 3), does not meet the bar (correctness 2, verification 2, median 2); fixable in one session by correcting the reuse and DRS rows, adding later-of notes and article numbers checked against CELEX 32025R0040, and pinning each duty's date and categories in a table test.
